post_wise_qualification.essential_qualification: Standard UGC 2018 Professor pattern (A or B): (A) An eminent scholar with a Ph.D. in the concerned/allied discipline, minimum 10 research publications in peer-reviewed/UGC-listed journals, a total research score of 120 (Appendix II, Table 2, UGC Regulations 2018), and minimum 10 years' teaching/research experience as Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor with evidence of successfully guiding a doctoral candidate; OR (B) An outstanding professional with a Ph.D. in the relevant/allied/applied discipline from any academic institution or industry, with significant contribution to the discipline supported by documentary evidence, and 10 years' experience.

Menpa Kachupa or Bachelor's Degree in Sowa-Rigpa (or equivalent recognised by erstwhile CCIM/NCISM); desirable: Menrampa or Postgraduate qualification in Sowa-Rigpa; valid State/Central/National registration under NCISM. Experience: 10 years as regular teacher or 5 years as Associate Professor/Reader for postgraduates; 13 years as regular teacher or 8 years as Associate Professor/Reader for undergraduates.

(A) An eminent scholar with a doctoral degree, minimum 10 years' research/teaching experience, minimum 6 research publications in peer-reviewed/UGC-listed journals, and a total research score of 120; OR (B) A traditional/professional artist with a Master's degree, "A" grade artist status of AIR/Doordarshan, 10 years of outstanding performing achievement, significant contributions and ability to guide research, participation in national/international seminars/conferences or award/fellowship recipient, and ability to teach theory with illustrations.

An eminent scholar with a Ph.D. or equivalent in Bhot Bauddha Darshan or Bauddha Darshan, minimum 10 research publications in peer-reviewed/UGC-listed journals, minimum 10 years' teaching/research experience (including editing, translation and restoration work with special reference to Buddhist Tantra) and a total research score of 120. Erudition in Tibetan/Sanskrit with knowledge of Hindi and English. Desirable: knowledge of ancient scripts (Newari, Bhujimol, Ranjana, etc.)/Apabhransh or Siddha Sahitya.

An eminent scholar with a Ph.D. in Bhot Bauddha Darshan/Tibetan Buddhist Philosophy or Sanskrit Bauddha Darshan, minimum 10 research publications in peer-reviewed/UGC-listed journals and a total research score of 120, minimum 10 years' teaching/research experience, and erudition in Tibetan/Sanskrit with knowledge of Hindi and English.

An eminent scholar with a Ph.D. or equivalent in Sanskrit Buddhist Studies, Tibetan Studies, or Sanskrit, minimum 10 research publications in peer-reviewed/UGC-listed journals and a total research score of 120, minimum 10 years' teaching/research experience with evidence of successfully guiding a doctoral candidate, and erudition in Sanskrit with knowledge of Bhoti and English. Tenure of 5 years. Age limit: below 65 years.

Good academic record with a Ph.D. in the concerned/allied discipline; a Master's Degree with at least 55% marks (or equivalent grade); minimum 8 years' teaching/research experience at Assistant Professor-equivalent level in a University/College/Accredited Research Institution or industry, with a minimum of 7 publications in peer-reviewed/UGC-listed journals and a total research score of 75 (Appendix II, Table 2, UGC Regulations 2018).

Good academic record with a Ph.D. in Bhot Bauddha Darshan/Tibetan Buddhist Philosophy; Master's Degree with at least 55% marks in the same subject; erudition in Tibetan and Sanskrit with knowledge of Hindi or English; minimum 8 years' experience in editing/restoration of Buddhist text or equivalent teaching/research experience, OR 12 years as Research Assistant; minimum 7 publications in peer-reviewed/UGC-listed/institute-recognised journals with a research score of 75.

Good academic record with a Ph.D. in Bhot Bauddha Darshan/Tibetan Buddhist Philosophy; Master's Degree with at least 55% marks in the same subject; erudition in Tibetan with knowledge of Sanskrit, Hindi or English; minimum 8 years' experience of translating Buddhist philosophical texts or equivalent teaching/research experience, OR 12 years as Research Assistant; minimum 7 publications with a research score of 75.

Postgraduate degree in Sciences, Mathematics, Social Sciences, Commerce or Languages; M.Ed.; Ph.D. in Education; 8 years' teaching experience in a teacher education institution; any other UGC-prescribed qualification. Desirable: Diploma/Degree in Educational Administration or Leadership.

Menpa Kachupa or Bachelor's Degree in Sowa-Rigpa (or equivalent recognised by erstwhile CCIM/NCISM); desirable: Menrampa/Postgraduate qualification in Sowa-Rigpa; valid registration under NCISM. Experience: 5 years' regular teaching for postgraduates, or 8 years' regular teaching for undergraduates.

Standard UGC Assistant Professor pattern (A or B): (A) A Master's degree with 55% marks (or equivalent grade) in the concerned/relevant/allied subject from an Indian University or accredited foreign university/Traditional Institution, AND the candidate must have cleared NET (UGC/CSIR) or an equivalent accredited test (SLET/SET), or hold a Ph.D. awarded under UGC (Minimum Standards) Regulations 2009/2016 (exempting NET/SLET/SET), subject to specified conditions (regular-mode Ph.D., thesis evaluated by two external examiners, open viva-voce, two published research papers with at least one in a refereed journal, and two conference presentations funded/sponsored by UGC/ICSSR/CSIR or similar, certified by the Registrar/Dean Academic Affairs); OR (B) A Ph.D. from a foreign university ranked in the world's top 500 (QS, THE, or ARWU Shanghai) - in which case shortlisting uses the Appendix II Table 3A academic score, but final selection is based purely on interview performance.

(A) Master's Degree with 55% marks (or equivalent grade) in the relevant subject from an Indian/foreign University, plus NET/SLET/SET clearance or a qualifying Ph.D. per UGC 2009/2016 Regulations (with the same conditions as above); OR (B) A traditional/professional artist with a Bachelor's degree who studied under a noted/reputed traditional Master/Artist, has been an "A" grade artist of AIR/Doordarshan, can explain the subject with logical reasoning, and has adequate knowledge to teach theory with illustrations.

Good academic record with a Ph.D. in Bhot Bauddha Darshan/Bauddha Darshan/Buddha Tantra; Master's Degree with at least 55% marks in Bhot Bauddha Darshan/Sanskrit Bauddha Darshan or a relevant discipline; erudition in Tibetan and Sanskrit with knowledge of Hindi or English. Desirable: knowledge of ancient scripts (Newari, Bhujimol, Ranjana, etc.)/Apabhransh or Siddha Sahitya.

Good academic record with a Ph.D. in Bhot Bauddha Darshan/Tibetan Buddhist Philosophy; Master's Degree with at least 55% marks in Bhot Bauddha Darshan; erudition in Tibetan with knowledge of Sanskrit, Hindi or English.

Good academic record with a Ph.D. in Bhot Bauddha Darshan/Tibetan Buddhist Philosophy; Master's Degree with at least 55% marks in Bhot Bauddha Darshan/Tibetan Buddhist Philosophy from an Indian University or accredited foreign university; erudition in Tibetan and Sanskrit with knowledge of Hindi and English.

Postgraduate degree in Education (M.Ed.) with minimum 55% marks or equivalent grade; NET or State-Level Eligibility Test, or Ph.D. in Education, or another UGC-prescribed qualification. Desirable: Master's degree in Psychology, Philosophy, Sociology or allied subjects.

Postgraduate degree in Tibetan Language and Literature with minimum 55% marks; B.Ed. with minimum 55% marks; NET/SLET or Ph.D. in Education or the concerned subject. Desirable: M.Ed. (with Specialisation) or Ph.D. in Education.

Postgraduate degree in Tibetan Buddhist Philosophy with minimum 55% marks; B.Ed. with minimum 55% marks; NET/SLET or Ph.D. in Education or the concerned subject. Desirable: M.Ed. (with Specialisation) or Ph.D. in Education.

Postgraduate degree in Hindi with minimum 55% marks; B.Ed. with minimum 55% marks; NET/SLET or Ph.D. in Education or the concerned subject. Desirable: M.Ed. (with Specialisation) or Ph.D. in Education.

Menpa Kachupa or Bachelor's Degree in Sowa-Rigpa (or equivalent recognised by erstwhile CCIM/NCISM); desirable: Menrampa/Postgraduate qualification in Sowa-Rigpa; valid registration under NCISM. No teaching experience is required, but a minimum of 2 years' professional experience is mandatory, and age must not exceed 45 years at the time of first appointment.

how_to_apply: Eligible and interested candidates must apply online only through the CIHTS recruitment portal, and additionally send a hard copy of the completed application by registered post.
Apply online at https://cihtsrec.samarth.edu.in between 08.09.2026 and 07.10.2026.
Upload a recent colour passport-size photograph, the applicant's signature, and all relevant documents on the portal.
Pay the requisite application fee online, where applicable.
After submitting the online application, print the completed application form.

Send the printed application form, along with self-attested copies of all uploaded enclosures, by registered post to: The Registrar, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Sarnath, Varanasi-221007 (U.P.), within 3 days from the last date of online submission.
The envelope must be superscribed with the advertisement number, the name of the post applied for, and the post code number and category.

No other means or mode of submission of applications will be accepted. Fields marked with an asterisk (*) on the online form are mandatory. Before clicking "Submit," candidates must ensure the information provided is correct and final, as no changes will be entertained after submission.
important_instructions: Candidates must have a valid email ID and mobile number for registration on the online application portal. Candidates are advised to regularly check the CIHTS website (www.cihts.ac.in) for further instructions or information. Candidates must indicate their caste/category in the appropriate column of the application form; leaving this column blank will not be treated as an application for the unreserved category, and the application will be rejected as incomplete. Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD) with disability less than 40% will not be considered against posts reserved for PwBD. Any subsequent change of address, telephone number, or email address must be promptly communicated to the Registrar, CIHTS, Sarnath. Candidates are advised to apply well in time to avoid last-minute rush. Incomplete or incorrect applications, in any respect, will be rejected. Canvassing in any form will render a candidate disqualified, and their application will be rejected. Any litigation in this matter is subject to Varanasi jurisdiction only. In case of any discrepancy, inconsistency, or difference in interpretation between the English and Hindi versions of the official notification, the English version shall prevail and be treated as final and authoritative.

faq.question: Q1. What is CIHTS Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is a recruitment drive by the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Sarnath, Varanasi, for 59 teaching posts of Professor, Associate Professor, and Assistant Professor across 40 subject/post combinations, under Advertisement No. CIHTS/Acad./Rectt./01/2026.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in CIHTS Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 59 total vacancies: 27 UR, 9 SC, 4 ST, 15 OBC, and 4 EWS, distributed across Professor, Associate Professor and Assistant Professor posts in various departments.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for CIHTS Recruitment 2026?
